translation: Long ago, at the beginning of the Kṛta age — and the gods [siramaisvaraiḥ: reading unanalyzable, corrupt in the source e-text].
All the gods deliberated upon the cause named Dāruka.

sanskrit: tacchrutvā hariḥ proktaḥ striyaṃ sṛṣṭiti tadvada ||
translation: Having heard that, Hari was told: 'Creation of a woman — speak thus.'
Brahmāṇī, born from Brahmā; Māheśvarī, (born) from Maheśvara.
Vārāhī, born from Yama; Indrāṇī, born from Indra.
The great demon would go to weakness of the Mothers at the hands of the mighty one.

translation: But indeed the one supreme portion (abides) in the eye of Parameśvara, the supreme Lord.
Having split the wooden heart — the blood smeared with flesh.

sanskrit: tacchrutvā īśvaro devī nṛttaṃ kṛtvā tu śāmyati ||
translation: Having heard that, the Lord becomes calm, the Goddess having performed a dance.

sanskrit: tāsāṃ vai mūrtibhedantu śṛṇu brahma yuge yuge ||
translation: Indeed, hear, O Brahmā, the distinction of their forms, in age after age.
Prakarālyā, Tīkṣṇākṣī ('sharp-eyed'), Vidyujjihvā ('lightning-tongued'), Vijṛmbhiṇī ('the expansive one').

sanskrit: adhomukhī ca vikhyātā tathā raudramukhī bhavet ||
translation: And the downward-faced (Adhomukhī) is well-known; likewise the fierce-faced (Raudramukhī) would be.

sanskrit: tryambakī gomukhī caiva snehākhyā ca tathā parā ||
translation: Tryambakī and Gomukhī, and she who is named Snehā, and likewise the supreme one (Parā).
And these forms are to be known, and they are proclaimed as the Mātṛkās.
The red and redder (shade) is to be known; the yellow and yellower (shade) should be (present).
And Bhadrakālī and Cāmuṇḍī are always victory-increasing (Vijayavardhinī).
By these, the forms are to be known; (this) should always be peace-effecting.
And indeed the ten peace-effecting ones should (bring) victory to kings.
And by the rite (vidhāna) of the fourfold seat (caturbhūti), he should cause the worship of the Mothers to be performed.

sanskrit: iti brahmayāmale śatasahasrasaṃhitāyāṃ mātrotsavo nāma prathamaḥ paṭalaḥ || 1
translation: Thus, in the Brahmayāmala, in the hundred-thousand(-verse) Saṃhitā, [ends] the first chapter (paṭala) named Mātrotsava, the Festival of the Mothers.

sanskrit: grāme ca nagare caiva pattane kheṭakepi ca ||
translation: And in a village, and also in a city, in a town (paṭṭana), and also in a market-town (kheṭaka) —

sanskrit: parvate ca vane caiva nadīnāṃ rājadhānike ||
translation: And on a mountain, and also in a forest, at the royal capital of the rivers —
And in the south — untimely death; and in the southwest — [one is] afflicted with disease.
In the Saumyā quarter — complete success; in the Aiśānya quarter — [that which] bestows the eight siddhis.
Having made an interval of a hundred daṇḍas — [it is] the supreme [ground] that effects all accomplishments.
But at the gate of Yama (south): strife; in the southwest one would meet with destruction.
Of these [doors], the northern door: sovereignty ever higher and higher.
Brahmin, kṣatriya, vaiśya, and indeed śūdra — the fourfold [division].
Red-eyed, large-eyed, red-haired, charming.
Holding the sword, the khaṭvāṅga and the śūla, and the axe in the right (hand).

sanskrit: pāṃsunā pūrayet tatra udakaṃ pūrayet purā ||
translation: In the left (hand) he should place the bracelet, having trodden on Dāruka with the foot.
And the two glances; serenity should be at the forehead; (the image is) endowed with radiance.
Thus the rite is to be performed: Ekavīrī, captivating.

sanskrit: iti brahmayāmale śatasahasrasaṃhitāyāṃ bhūparigraho nāma dvitīyaḥ paṭalaḥ || 2
translation: Having placed Caṇḍākṣī in the west, one should place (her) north of Mahocchiṣṭa.

sanskrit: śailajā lohajā caiva ratnajā maṇinā śubhā ||
translation: Having performed (it) with the rite seen in the śāstra, one should arrange (them) in the corners.
These, indeed, (placed) at the door-region; one should place the door-guardian in order.
Midway between Aindra (the east) and Īśāna (the northeast) should be the abode of Kṣetrapāla.
Having dug gold there, (one proceeds) with the rite seen (in) the rule (vidhi).
And the lesser (measure) should be half of that; that is declared threefold.

sanskrit: bhāgaikantu bhavet pīṭhaṃ tadardhena tu nirṇaye ||
translation: First the front (agra) is to be made, endowed with its characteristic mark.
One should cast the five jewels there; and, indeed, below — (says) the wise one.
Five single (units) apart from that, with the nine-syllable (mantra), in due order.
Equal to the width is declared, and the height too, (all) with the characteristic mark.

sanskrit: hṛdayaṃ nābhideśe tu mukhaṃ tatraiva cocyate ||
translation: First, square, endowed with the characteristic mark.
But the corner, having been made fivefold, that one part should be threefold.
Having made (it) an equal square, above the round (base) the square (part).
There, (in) one part — but (that) part — one should make the lotus, with its characteristic mark.
Thus having made (it) in brief, the pīṭha, indeed, is charming.
In sprinkling (prokṣaṇa), and in installation (pratiṣṭhā), in the festival (utsava), or also in the bathing (snapana)...
The vessel is declared fourfold in the aṅkura (sprout) rite.
Golden, silver, copper, bronze, indeed, and earthen — or (any of these).
But the conch-shaped (vessel): the conch's (measure is) round and eight aṅgulas.
At the tip, shaped like a lotus petal, furnished with eight petals.

sanskrit: caturbhujaṃ triṇetraṃ ca śiro mālā vibhūṣitā ||
translation: Sixteen aṅgulas in length; and indeed the length of three parts.
And indeed the water (part is) three aṅgulas, and the belly ten aṅgulas.
The śarāva is eighteen aṅgulas in height, free of cracks.
The ghaṭikā is eighteen aṅgulas in length; (its) pañcatrika (measure).
And the kumbha (jar): eight aṅgulas in girth (nāha); the mouth should be four aṅgulas.

sanskrit: vāme tu kaṭakaṃ dadyāt pādenākramya dārukān ||
translation: Sixteen aṅgulas (in) width, and its mouth — (text breaks off: * * * *).
For that purpose (is) the width of the neck; for that purpose the aperture (bila) is declared.
I will declare the rule of the pavilion (maṇḍapa) for the maṅgalāṅkura rite.
For the Kṣatriya, nine hastas; and for the Vaiśya, eight hastas.
Thirty-six — sixteen pillars; and indeed twelve pillars.

sanskrit: etā vai dvāradeśe tu dvārapālaṃ nyaset kramāt ||
translation: Having made (it) an equal square, resembling the surface of a mirror.
Furnished with four arches (toraṇas), beautified with banners in the eight directions.

sanskrit: svarṇantatra khanitvā tu vidhi dṛṣṭena karmaṇā ||
translation: (Marked with) the banyan, udumbara, and aśvattha — with (these) trees and so on, in order.
Five hastas in length is declared; the width (is) its vihasta (measure).
White, red, so too black, and gray, and the vāruṇa (color), likewise.

sanskrit: pañcaratnaṃ kṣipet tatra tvadho caiva vicakṣaṇaḥ ||
translation: On the canopy — and above, wondrous, adorned with (pendants at the) neck and cāmaras (chowries).
Having wrapped the pillars, afterwards (the pavilion is) adorned with sprouts (pallava).

sanskrit: vistārasya samaṃ proktaṃ cotsedhañca sa lakṣaṇaṃ ||
translation: Having done thus — but first — then one should begin the aṅkura (sprout rite).
But with rice — with ten droṇas, or with half of that, (or) with half of that.
